pageTitle: Klacks for the UK | Rostering for Private Care and Security

hero.badge: For private care homes, security providers and facilities management in the UK
hero.titleHtml: Opt-out records for the 48-hour week — on file, not on request.
hero.subtitle: The Working Time Regulations 1998 require a written, freely revocable opt-out for the 48-hour week, which employers must be able to evidence. With high staff turnover and expensive bank and agency shifts, that record-keeping is the real pain point — Klacks is deliberately built for the private sector, not the NHS.
hero.screenshotCaption: Screenshot shown in German — the core app interface ships in German, English, French and Italian; the Klacksy AI assistant additionally understands English.

challenges.eyebrow: The everyday reality of private care, security & FM
challenges.title: Opt-out paperwork and expensive short-notice cover

items.title: Opt-out record-keeping
items.text: Every 48-hour-week opt-out needs to be in writing and evidenced — with high staff turnover, that's a growing administrative burden.

items.title: Expensive bank and agency shifts
items.text: Short-notice cover through agency staff or internal bank pools is often the costliest option — better forward planning reduces how often you need it.

items.title: High turnover in the private sector
items.text: Private care homes, security providers and FM teams all deal with staff turnover that makes manual rotas go stale fast.

openSource.title: Full data sovereignty: open source & on-premise
openSource.text: Klacks was built for sectors with strict security and compliance requirements, where sensitive staff data should never leave your own infrastructure. As an open-source solution, Klacks can run entirely in your own data centre or on secured local servers — without depending on US cloud providers. That makes UK GDPR and ICO compliance entirely your own responsibility to manage, not a vendor's.
bullets: On-premise sovereignty: full control over rosters, opt-out records and logs within your own IT environment.
Open LLM architecture: AI-assisted scheduling suggestions can also run on locally hosted language models, so no data ever leaves for external APIs.
Auditable source code: a fully inspectable codebase for IT audits and internal compliance reviews.

solutions.title: How Klacks handles opt-out records and short-notice cost
solutions.subtitle: Deliberately built for the private sector — no NHS ESR integration, so you're up and running fast.

items.title: Recovery Engine for absences
items.text: If a staff member calls in sick, Klacks instantly finds the best-qualified internal replacement — before an expensive bank or agency shift becomes necessary.

items.title: Opt-out tracking
items.text: Klacks tracks each employee's opt-out status and average weekly hours continuously — on file whenever HR needs to check.

items.title: BrightPay-compatible payroll export
items.text: Finished hours, overtime and allowances export directly in a format ready for BrightPay, widely used across the UK and Ireland.

items.title: Autofill wizard for rotations
items.text: The GA-powered autofill assistant plans shift rotations while respecting the working-time limits on file.

items.title: Qualification-aware scheduling
items.text: Only staff with a matching qualification and a valid security or care licence are ever suggested for a shift.

klacksy.title: Klacksy: the assistant built into your team's workflow
klacksy.text: Klacksy isn't a bolted-on marketing chatbot — it's embedded directly in the Klacks interface. Staff and schedulers ask about shifts via chat, request shift swaps, or resolve qualification conflicts within the team. A built-in skills and rules system ensures Klacksy only ever suggests changes that actually match the qualifications and working-time limits of the people involved.
